record.original_question: Find a class of nonnegative majorants μ on [−1,1] for which the associated snake polynomials have a Chebyshev expansion whose coefficients are either all nonnegative or sign-alternating.

evidence.quote: Problem 7.1 (Geno Nikolov). Find a class of majorants µ for which the associated snake polynomials have non-negative (or sign-alternating) expansion in the Chebyshev polynomials of the first kind.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let μ : [−1, 1] → [0, ∞) be a nonnegative function (a "majorant"). For each integer n ≥ 1, an associated "snake polynomial" of degree n is a real algebraic polynomial P_n of degree n which is extremal in the sense that it oscillates between ±μ on [−1, 1]: there exist points −1 ≤ x_0 < x_1 < … < x_n ≤ 1 such that P_n(x_k) = (−1)^{n−k} μ(x_k) for k = 0, 1, …, n (so the graph of P_n weaves like a snake between the curves y = μ(x) and y = −μ(x)). Each such polynomial admits a unique expansion
P_n(x) = Σ_{k=0}^{n} a_{n,k} T_k(x),
where T_k denotes the Chebyshev polynomial of the first kind of degree k.

Problem: Identify a class C of nonnegative majorants μ on [−1, 1] such that, for every μ ∈ C and every n ≥ 1, the Chebyshev coefficients {a_{n,k}}_{k=0}^{n} of the associated snake polynomial P_n are either all nonnegative or alternate in sign (i.e., (−1)^{n−k} a_{n,k} ≥ 0 for all k).
artifact.status_search_result: No published resolution of this problem was found in a web search. It is posed as an open question by G. Nikolov in a recent open-problems compilation, and no later work reporting a complete or partial answer was located.

status_evidence.snippet: Related work by Nikolov on Chebyshev polynomial inequalities; no resolution of the snake-polynomial majorant question.
status_evidence.claim: No solution to the stated majorant/snake-polynomial problem appears in this related work.

status_evidence.snippet: Surveys Markov-type and snake-polynomial extremal problems with majorants.
status_evidence.claim: Surveys related extremal problems but does not resolve the Chebyshev-coefficient sign question.
